gap.name: Paley of primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4)
gap.why_gpu: The full N×N difference tensor and batched modular exponentiation are one CUDA kernel.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001's 40% Paley slice: primes p ∈ [17, 997] only. This is the baseline, not a gap.
gap.growth: N = p ≈ k^2 (sub-exponential). Paley of order p has ω,α ~ √p.

gap.name: Paley of prime powers F_{p^n}, n>1
gap.kernel: batched F_{p^2} multiply-exponentiate on outer differences
gap.why_gpu: Field arithmetic is a uniform (re, im) tensor; no Python-level per-edge loop.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001 spec: Paley restricted to primes p ∈ [17,997]. Prime-power Paley (q=9,25,49,121,169,289,…) was never generated.
gap.growth: Same Paley clique heuristic ω~√q, but denser parameter lattice than primes alone.

gap.name: Generalized Paley GP(p,k), k-th power residues, k>2
gap.why_gpu: Identical kernel to Paley with a different exponent; cubic/quartic/sextic families are free on GPU.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001 encoded algebraic residues as a 10-bit quadratic/cyclotomic sketch, but adjacency was quadratic Paley only. Cubic Paley (Clapham) and GP(p,4), GP(p,6) were not enumerated.
gap.growth: sparser than Paley (degree (p-1)/k). Used in the literature for R(7,7) and multicolour R_k(4).

gap.name: Cyclotomic class-union Cayley graphs
gap.why_gpu: Once dlog[0..p) lives in device memory, every mask is a broadcast compare. Sweeping 2^{e/2} negation-closed subsets is embarrassingly parallel.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Task 4 asked to search cyclotomic classes guided by Random Forest importance. Artifacts show family-correlation CSVs, not a GPU mask sweep of index-e class unions.
gap.growth: Contains Paley (e=2) and GP as special cases; extra masks can beat Paley at the same p.

gap.name: Quadratic-form Cayley graphs on F_2^n
gap.kernel: XOR outer product + bitwise quadratic form
gap.why_gpu: The most GPU-native kernel in the catalogue: N=2^n vertices, adjacency[i,j] = Q(i xor j). Maps to CUDA bitwise ops with no modular arithmetic.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001's algebraic graphs were Paley/Frankl–Wilson/NLFSR over odd-characteristic fields. Affine polar / symplectic quadrics over F_2 were absent.
gap.growth: Strongly regular for nondegenerate Q. N doubles with each bit; k grows much slower than log N.

gap.name: Gold / trace-of-power sequence graphs on F_2^n
gap.kernel: XOR outer + GF(2^n) power + Frobenius trace
gap.why_gpu: m-sequence / Gold / Kasami evaluation is a linear-feedback (or carry-less multiply) kernel. GPUs already do this for cryptography and CDMA.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: NLFSR-Ramsey in Run001 used nonlinear feedback shift registers as an algebraic construction, almost certainly on CPU for tiny n. The linear Gold/Kasami siblings — which are the actual GPU bread-and-butter — were not batched.
gap.growth: Related to bent and almost-bent functions; clique size tied to the degree of the trace polynomial.

gap.name: Orthogonal polarity graphs of PG(2,q)
gap.kernel: point enumeration + GEMM of homogeneous coordinates (x·y ≡ 0)
gap.why_gpu: Adjacency is a batched dot product — one cuBLAS GEMM plus a modulus compare. N = q^2+q+1.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001 stayed on diagonal Paley/FW hybrids. Polarity graphs of projective planes (and GQ polarity graphs used by Mattheus–Verstraete for R(4,t)) were not built.
gap.growth: Off-diagonal strength is the point: triangle structure is geometric, not random. GPU makes a q-sweep cheap.

gap.name: Nagy intersecting-family graphs
gap.why_gpu: Vertices are 2-subsets; intersection size is a bitwise popcount of an AND table — a textbook GPU reduction.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Classical explicit cubic construction R(t,t) > binom(t,2). Not in the 40/30/20/10 Paley/FW/synthetic/DIMACS mix.
gap.growth: N = t(t-1)/2 with ω,α ≤ t, so N ~ k^2/2 — same polynomial regime as Paley, fully explicit.

gap.name: Strong products / Kronecker lifts of certified seeds
gap.why_gpu: Kronecker products are GPU BLAS. Lifting Paley(17)⊠Paley(17) is one call.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001 generated atoms, not recursive Abbott-style product families. No tensor/XOR/lexicographic lift appears in the listed CSVs.
gap.growth: ω(G⊠G) ≤ (ω(G)+1)^2-style bounds; N squares. Explicit infinite family from any single seed.

gap.name: Singer difference-set circulants (PG(2,q))
gap.kernel: circulant broadcast of a (q^2+q+1, q+1, 1) difference set
gap.why_gpu: A circulant is one row rolled N times — a gather kernel. Linear m-sequences generating Singer sets are LFSR steps, GPU-trivial.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001 explored NLFSR (nonlinear) algebraic graphs for Erdős 78. The linear Singer/m-sequence circulants that GPUs already generate as PN sequences were not certified as Ramsey graphs.
gap.growth: Degree q+1 on N=q^2+q+1 vertices; strongly regular (lattice of the projective plane).

gap.name: Block-circulant / two-block Cayley search
gap.kernel: batched circulant blocks + GPU local search / SAT
gap.why_gpu: Exoo–McKay-style R(5,5) searches and the DSC-3 Galois cycle-type annealer are GPU iterated local search over connection sets.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Run001's RL task (PPO edge flips, GNN attention) was specified and then cut by the 100 GPU-hour budget. No gnn_model.pt appears in the Run001 artifact list. Block-circulant SAT for R(5,5) was never started.
gap.growth: Cell-wise (small Ramsey numbers), not an exponential diagonal family — but it is the GPU construction the compute budget was supposed to buy.

gap.name: PPO edge-flip + GAT θ/K-free training
gap.kernel: PyTorch Geometric GAT + PPO on adjacency Bernoulli actions
gap.why_gpu: This is the named GPU workload of RamseyConstructor-GNN (Tasks 2–3).
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Deliverables required gnn_model.pt. The listed Run001 files have RF/algebraic CSVs and Kosmos specs, not a trained GAT or PPO policy. Classification/regression targets (F1≥0.80, MSE≤1.0) were never reported from a GPU training run.
gap.growth: A search heuristic, not a parametric family. GPU-necessary, not GPU-sufficient — Berghaus–Wagner ICLR 2025 found RL can lose to random on R(4,4).

gap.name: GPU Lovász ϑ SDP (randomized / CVXPY)
gap.kernel: SDP on GPU, or randomized sketch of the theta body
gap.why_gpu: Task 5 Tier 3: ϑ(Ḡ) as an upper bound on ω(G), budgeted at 500 graphs on A100.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Budget reconciliation replaced ϑ with Hoffman/spectral proxies for all but a sampled 500. No verification_log.json / benchmark_log.json in the listed artifacts, so the GPU SDP subset likely did not ship.
gap.growth: Does not build graphs; certifies them. GPU still unused relative to the spec.

gap.name: GEMM clique counting (A³, neighborhood A³)
gap.why_gpu: trace(A³)/6 and per-neighborhood K4 are pure matrix multiplies. Exact ω for N≤200 was assigned to CPU cliquer.
gap.why_skipped_or_done: Tier 1 used cliquer on N≤200; Tier 2 MiniSat on ≤200 graphs; Tier 3 spectral proxies. Batched GEMM certification — the obvious GPU replacement for cliquer — was not used.
gap.growth: Enables k-freeness checks on the GPU constructions above at N up to a few hundred.
